static_traits.name: Chen Yu
static_traits.social_status: Having a few close friends to confide in, but not yet fully expressing negative thoughts to them
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; not yet received psychotherapy before; psychological distress appearing after the first divorce
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly organized; steady speech rate; fair cooperativeness but rather negative attitude, skeptical; limited self-disclosure (worrying about burdening friends); shy and tending to avoid socializing

basic_info.main_problem: Since the divorce, continuously feeling despair and negativity, doubting the possibility of finding love again.
basic_info.core_demands: These negative thoughts have affected my mental health and hindered me from moving on from the divorce, and I hope to change them through counseling.
growth_experiences: Experienced the first divorce six months ago, with negative emotions (despair, negativity) appearing almost immediately after the divorce and persisting; repeatedly reinforcing the thought 'I will not find love again' when seeing happy couples in public; seeing parents with children at work triggering pain about losing family; shyness making it hard to actively meet new friends; trying to distract by throwing oneself into work and social activities, but negative thinking frequently returning; sleep affected (difficulty falling asleep, repeatedly thinking about the divorce at night); although having a few close friends, rarely sharing deeply due to not wanting to 'burden others'.

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of being loved
I am destined to be Loneliness

special_situations.event: Seeing happy couples in public places
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am unable to have a stable intimate relationship like them, it means I am unlovable or a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding socializing situations or choosing Being alone to avoid triggering comparison and frustration
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never have such a relationship again

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot have a family and intimate relationship, the divorce means I am permanently labeled unlovable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Putting more energy into work to distract, but still repeatedly thinking about loss and loneliness inside
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have lost all this and will not have it in the future

special_situations.event: Being alone at night, repeatedly thinking about the divorce when trying to fall asleep
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get rid of these feelings and thoughts soon, life will always be terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Suppresses thoughts by working overtime or staying busy, avoiding facing emotions directly
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My life has been permanently branded 'unlovable' by the divorce

special_situations.event: When considering actively meeting new friends or using dating apps
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I appear shy or get rejected, it proves I am not worthy of being loved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding trying socializing or dating due to shyness, lowering the chance of being rejected
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will look down on me / no one will respond to me

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be loved and accepted, to build a stable intimate relationship and family
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and hurt again, worrying about being permanently labeled 'unlovable' and falling into loneliness
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being rejected and lowering emotional exposure by keeping distance and staying busy, to protect fragile self-esteem and safety

object_relations.self_representation: A person branded by divorce as 'unlovable and lonely'
object_relations.object_representation: Others (especially potential partners) are seen as possible rejecters or judges

object_relations.self_representation: A bystander who has lost family and intimacy
object_relations.object_representation: Happy couples in public places and parents/children at work are regarded as 'the havers in the outside world'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes challenging the belief 'I will not find love again' through behavioral experiments and cognitive restructuring
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to emphasize with rational reasons that methods may be ineffective (such as 'I have been stuck for a long time'), to reduce emotional exposure and uncertainty
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expresses doubt in a calm, rational tone, emphasizing past persistent predicaments as arguments, avoiding in-depth discussion of emotional experience and vulnerability.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests sharing feelings with close friends and seeking social support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding 'seeking support' as burdening the other, thus negating the availability of external support
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Politely but firmly refusing to ask outward for help, using the expression 'I do not want to trouble others', maintaining a self-enclosed and self-reliant posture.

manifestations: Repeatedly having the thoughts 'I will always be alone' / 'no one will love me again' after the divorce
Shyness making it hard to meet new friends
Not yet fully sharing true feelings with friends to avoid 'burdening them'
outcomes: Social avoidance and blocked relationship expansion

manifestations: Feeling 'trying is pointless' / 'what is the point', feeling empty about life goals and intimate-relationship prospects
Seeing family and intimate interactions triggering loss and emptiness

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Taking 'cannot trouble others' as the rule, avoiding seeking support from friends
Internalizing the external evaluation of 'being divorced = unlovable' as a self-label

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Choosing to bear it alone despite knowing outside support is needed
Turning the impulse to meet new friends into self-repression and Being alone
Pressures himself with overtime and busyness rather than seeking external help

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Describing oneself as 'unlovable' in a self-denial way
Excessively worrying about others' evaluations before attempting socializing, thus reducing action

positive_force: Has a stable job and a master's degree, with some occupational functioning and a structured life
Has several close friends as potential support resources
Willing to seek professional help, though skeptical, willing to try
Able to identify and express one's own automatic thoughts and troubles, with some self-awareness
negative_force: Shyness and social avoidance, reducing contact and trial opportunities
Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and mind reading reinforcing negative anticipation
Persistent despair and insomnia triggered by the divorce event, weakening resilience
The core belief 'I am not worthy of being loved' leading to self-denial and low self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Social and dating avoidance, choosing Being alone
antecedent: Seeing happy couples in public places
Seeing parents with children at work
Thinking about actively meeting new friends or using dating apps
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'I am not worthy of being loved / I will always be alone' formed after divorce and the fear of being rejected; shy temperament and negative automatic thoughts (mind-reading, catastrophizing) driving avoidance
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome emotions (shame, fear, grief) and anticipated rejection, maintaining safety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Blocked relationship expansion, worsened loneliness, difficulty recovering from divorce, work and decreased quality of life

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly thinking about the divorce at night causing insomnia (rumination)
antecedent: Being alone at night, when trying to fall asleep
Emotions triggered during the day continuing into the night
target_behavior.core_reason: A rumination tendency and emotional reasoning and overgeneralization for understanding and controlling traumatic events; uses thinking in place of emotional processing
target_behavior.function: Tries to gain mastery and explanation through thinking, while avoiding directly experiencing painful emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Declining sleep quality, impaired self-care, next-day fatigue and reduced work efficiency

target_behavior.behavior: Distracts herself by staying busy / over-investing in work
antecedent: When feeling despair or being overwhelmed by negative thoughts
When facing pressure from intimate and social situations
target_behavior.core_reason: Using busyness as a compensatory strategy to avoid facing loss and loneliness
target_behavior.function: Reducing emotional intensity short-term, avoiding inner pain
target_behavior.consequence: Only short-term relief, hard to fundamentally improve the problem, long-term fatigue and decreased motivation, negative thinking still recurring
